newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australian Broadcasting Corp Morning Update.
newsitem.headline: Australian Broadcasting Corp Morning Update.

text.p: TODDLER SEARCH CONTINUES IN GIPPSLAND
The boyfriend of a Victorian woman who's toddler disappeared on Sunday morning is to provide police with blood samples as part of an investigation into the disappearance.
It was confirmed yesterday that Jaidyn Leski's mother Belinda Murphy and her boyfriend Greg Domaszewicz spent the day in Melbourne with a solicitor.
Police say Mr Domaszewicz has agreed to provide blood samples, after seeking legal advice.
Meanwhile, police will again speak with family members in the Moe region and will continue searching Lake Naraccan to try and find signs of the missing boy.
Investigators say they are worried about the toddler's safety, but hope that somebody has Jaidyn and is looking after him.
REAL-ESTATE STANDOVER TACTICS CLAIMED IN SYDNEY
Claims of a cartel operating in Sydney to stop discount real estate firms from advertising have been referred to the Australian Competition and Consumer Commission.
NSW Fair Trading Minister Faye Lo Po says she's concerned about allegations of an apparent cartel operating in Sydney's eastern suburbs.
The allegations are that eastern suburbs real estate agents threatened a local newspaper with closure if it carried ads for a discount real estate service.
Mrs Lo Po says if the practice is found to be anti competitive then her government will investigate further and collect the data that it needs to prosecute.
VIC HOSPITAL DISPUTES CONTINUE
Two disputes disrupting Victorian hospital services look set to continue, with nurses and other hospital workers maintaining their industrial action.
Unions say walk-outs and bans will continue at Victorian hospitals as non medical workers try to fight contracting out, and 35 hospitals are now involved in the action.
The Health Services Union says five hospitals a day are joining the action, which started at the Inner and Eastern Network.
There's also no end in sight to a week long nurses dispute.
Up to 500 beds have now been closed at a range of hospitals with elective surgery cancelled for the third day in a row.
Talks are continuing in the Industrial Relations Commission. - - - -
FORMER PREMIER HEADS FOR CANBERRA
Former Queensland Premier Wayne Goss says he wants to play a role in rebuilding Australia's relations with Asia if he succeeds in his push to be elected to Federal Parliament.
He's confirmed he'll seek preselection for a Federal seat but won't say which one until a redistribution of Federal boundaries is completed.
One seat he's considering is Rankin, to be vacated by former Labor Minister David Beddall.
Mr Goss says Australia was starting to progress in terms of its acceptance in Asia but that's been stalled by John Howard's failure to pull Pauline Hanson into line.
DON'T POLITICISE GAMES, WARNS MINISTER
The Federal Government has warned its New South Wales counterpart, and the Sydney Organising Committee for the Olympic Games, not to turn the games into a political event.
The New South Wales Government and Olympic organisers are at loggerheads over a 10 percent bed tax, with hotels refusing to sign contracts unless the bedtax is excluded.
That's further strained relations between SOCOG and the Carr Government - prompting federal tourism minister John Moore to issue a reminder that the games must not be politicised.
Speaking at an international travel trade fair in Melbourne, Mr Moore criticised the bed tax, saying New South Wales Premier Bob Carr will live to regret it.
-- Reuters Sydney Newsroom 61-2 9373-1800
